verses.1: The word of the LORD came to me in the seventh year, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, saying:
verses.2: "Son of man, write for yourself the name of this day, this very day. The king of Babylon has set his siege against Jerusalem on this very day.
verses.3: And speak a parable to the house of the rebel and say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: "Put on the pot, put it on, and also pour water into it.
verses.4: Collect its pieces to it, every good piece—thigh and shoulder, choice bones filled with marrow.
verses.5: Choose the choice of the flock and also a choice of the bones beneath it. Boil its bones in it.
verses.6: Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD: "Woe, the city of blood, the pot that has its scum in it and its scum has not gone out from it. It poured out its scum to its pieces. It did not fall upon it by lot.
verses.7: For its blood is in it, and it placed it on a smooth stone. It did not pour it out on the ground to cover it with dust.
verses.8: To raise up wrath to take vengeance, I have placed its blood on a smooth stone so it would not be covered.
verses.9: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Woe, the city of blood, I will greatly increase the uproar.
verses.10: Multiply the wood, kindle the fire, burn the meat and reduce the broth. Its bones will become charred.
verses.11: And set it on its coals, so that it may grow hot and heat up, its bronze may grow hot, and it may burn in its uncleanness, and its scum may be burned off.
verses.12: Its scum will not go out from it. Its scum will be burned in fire, its scum.
verses.13: Because of your impurity I have stirred up wrath, and though I have cleansed you, you have not been cleansed. You will not be cleansed again until I have spent My fury on you.
verses.14: I am the LORD. I have spoken, and I will do it. I will not delay, nor will I have mercy, nor will I have compassion, but according to your ways and according to your devices I will judge you," says the Lord GOD.
verses.15: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.16: "Son of man, behold, I am taking away from you the delight of your eyes with a stroke. You will not mourn, nor will you weep, and your eyes will not shed tears.
verses.17: A mourning for the dead, a lamentation, you will not make. Your turban will not be on your head, and your sandals will be on your feet, and you will not cover your face. You will not eat the bread of men.
verses.18: And I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening. And I did in the morning as I had been commanded.
verses.19: Then they said to me, "Will you not explain to us what these are, what you are doing?"
verses.20: And I said to them, "The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
verses.21: "Say to the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: "Behold, I will profane My sanctuary, the pride of your might, the delight of your eyes, and the soothing of your soul, and your sons and your daughters whom you have forsaken will fall by the sword.
verses.22: And you will do as I have done. You will not cover your face, nor eat the bread of men.
verses.23: And your hair on your heads and your sandals on your feet you will not mourn. You will not weep, and you will be stricken with your iniquities, and you will groan every man against his brother.
verses.24: And Ezekiel will be a sign to you. As I have done, so you will do, and you will know that I am the Lord GOD."
verses.25: And you, son of man, were you not the day I took away from them their strength, the pride of their rejoicing, the delight of their eyes and the soothing of their soul, their sons and their daughters?
verses.26: On that day a fugitive will come to you to bring you news to hear with ears.
verses.27: On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive, and you will speak, and you will no longer be stopped, and you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD."

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "reduce the broth" (וְהַרְקַח הַמֶּרְקָחָה) — the Hebrew is somewhat unclear, but I have taken it to mean "reduce the broth" based on the context of boiling and burning.
- v. 12: "its scum will be burned in fire, its scum" — the repetition of "scum" in the Hebrew emphasizes the uncleanness that remains.
- v. 25: "were you not the day I took away from them..." — the Hebrew uses a rhetorical question to emphasize the speaker's role in the events described.
- v. 26-27: "fugitive" (פָּלִיט) — the term refers to someone who escapes and brings news, likely a messenger from the besieged city.
